A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same OrderChain study, with corresponding text, equations, figures, and tables. Neither contains an appendix. Both mention a separate Supplemental Document that is absent from the supplied PDFs; the comparison covers the supplied material.

before.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–5 report original OrderChain evaluations on four ordinal regression tasks and component ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–5 retain the original four-task evaluations and component ablation results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same task-aware prompts, range optimization Chain-of-Thought, category recursive division, and LoRA-finetuned LLaVA. Renaming the initial step from formatting to identifying and transforming the input restates the previously described procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Adience age estimation, HCI historical image dating, image aesthetics assessment, and diabetic retinopathy grading. The represented categories, populations, and task requirements remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical comparator membership within each dataset, including zero-shot and finetuned LLaVA. Changes to citation numbers do not introduce or remove evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same dataset descriptions and split references, LLaVA-1.5-7B backbone, LoRA setup, learning rate of 2e-4, and batch size of 16. Accuracy and MAE remain the evaluation metrics; no new protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 5 retain the same Adience ablations of domain knowledge prompts, category feature prompts, and RO-CoT. The facial-age example in Figure 5 is unchanged, and no additional robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. Table 5's parenthetical values remain differences from the baseline, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–5 and Figure 2 match. OrderChain retains accuracy/MAE of 93.2%/0.12 on Adience, 73.0%/0.32 on HCI, 73.83%/0.260 overall on aesthetics, and 85.7%/0.23 on DR. Rankings and reported findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The ordered-label formulation in Section 3.1 and recursive-division equations (1)–(4) in Section 3.3 are unchanged. Equation (4) shifts between columns through text reflow; no definition, derivation, assumption, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty, unified ordinal regression, and performance claims. The title's new emphasis on instruct-tuning does not establish a different contribution; fine-tuning was already documented in v1.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations concerning subjective aesthetic labels, the People category, and robustness to DR class imbalance. Section 5 preserves the same limitations concerning subjective labels and zero-shot transfer to unseen domains.

D1.justification: The prompt examples and implementation disclosures remain the same, including PyTorch, the A100 GPU, backbone and encoder, LoRA, optimizer, and hyperparameters. Both retain the same reference to an unavailable separate Supplemental Document; no new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The introductory model examples are refreshed, but Section 2's literature coverage and the positioning against prior ordinal regression and CoT methods remain unchanged. The additional bibliography entry duplicates the already cited GPT-4 technical report as v2 references [1] and [2], rather than adding a distinct work.

P1.justification: The title changes from a general prompting paradigm to general instruct-tuning. The opening introduction paragraph and several method descriptions and step labels are locally rewritten, while the section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with separate input/output blocks, simplified grouping, revised arrows, Arabic step numbering, and an updated caption. Other figures and table structures remain unchanged; accompanying column and page reflow is limited.

improvement.justification: Figure 3 makes input/output separation more explicit, while the title and prose revisions mostly restate existing information. Awkward new wording in Sections 1 and 3.2 and a duplicated GPT-4 reference limit the editorial gains. With the scientific explanation, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations substantively unchanged, these local edits produce no meaningful net change in overall quality.
